section_summary: This section documents food supply and rationing conditions in occupied Japan between June 1948 and February 1949, focusing on staple and non-staple distribution, imports, price controls, and ration revisions. It features SCAP press statements and public releases reporting improved crop prospects, Egyptian rice shipments, and controls over perishable commodities, alongside congressional correspondence concerning an agricultural proposal by a Japanese-American constituent. The predominant subject is the controversial SCAP proposal to abolish supplementary food rations for foreign residents, including extensive petitions and comparative statistical studies from the International Committee of Kobe, French diplomatic endorsement, and State Department evaluations of the resulting financial and policy ramifications.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting SCAP's proposed discontinuance of supplementary food rations for foreign nationals in Japan and discussing objections raised by foreign missions.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports that SCAP is considering discontinuing supplementary food rations for foreign residents due to improved Japanese rations and U.S. financial costs. He details objections from the Chinese Mission and Kobe occidental residents, the potential financial burden if 600,000 Korean residents become eligible, and recommendations from SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section. The Mission suggests foreign governments provide their own funds if they wish to supply additional foods for their nationals.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 63: Supplementary Food Rations for Foreign Nationals in Japan

subfiles.about: Appeal from the International Committee of Kobe to SCAP protesting reductions in supplementary food rations for occidental residents, accompanied by three comparative statistical tables.
subfiles.from: International Committee of Kobe (U. A. Casal, W. A. McIlwaine, P. Boerstedt)
subfiles.summary: The International Committee of Kobe appeals to SCAP against severe reductions in supplementary food rations for occidental residents, arguing that rations are nutritionally inadequate and economically unaffordable under prevailing inflation. Three attached tables provide comparative statistical documentation: Table A details ration cuts between 1945 and 1948, Table B contrasts Japanese rations with British austerity rations, and Table C compares official commodity prices with local occupation wages.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Tokyo Despatch No. 63: Letter from the International Committee of Kobe to SCAP with Tables A, B, and C
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (through Chief of Diplomatic Section)

subfiles.about: Letter from the International Committee of Kobe soliciting support from foreign diplomatic missions in Tokyo against supplementary food ration cuts.
subfiles.from: International Committee of Kobe (U. A. Casal, W. A. McIlwaine, P. Boerstedt)
subfiles.summary: The International Committee of Kobe appeals to foreign diplomatic missions in Tokyo to intervene with SCAP on behalf of pre-war occidental residents facing severe food shortages and inflation. The letter contrasts the hardships of impoverished long-term residents and refugees with privileged post-war arrivals, urging diplomatic assistance to secure adequate rations, price relief, or purchasing privileges at the Overseas Supply Store. It stresses that occidental residents cannot survive on traditional Japanese diets without supplemental foods.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Tokyo Despatch No. 63: Explanatory Letter from the International Committee of Kobe to Heads of Diplomatic Missions in Tokyo
subfiles.to: Heads of Diplomatic Missions in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Memorandum from the French Mission in Japan to the Diplomatic Section supporting the appeal of the International Committee of Kobe.
subfiles.from: French Mission in Japan (Mission Française au Japon)
subfiles.summary: The French Mission endorses the Kobe committee's appeal, urging improved distribution of food facilities for foreign nationals residing in Japan.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Tokyo Despatch No. 63: Memorandum from the French Mission in Japan to the Diplomatic Section, GHQ, SCAP

subfiles.about: Intra-headquarters check sheet from ESS recommending termination of supplementary food rations for foreign nationals effective April 1, 1949.
subfiles.from: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP (ESS)
subfiles.summary: ESS check sheet recommending complete elimination of supplementary food rations for foreign nationals effective April 1, 1949, citing improved food conditions and potential $40,000,000 costs for Korean residents.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 4 to Tokyo Despatch No. 63: GHQ SCAP Check Sheet on Elimination of Supplementary Ration for Foreign Nationals
subfiles.to: Diplomatic Section, GHQ, SCAP (thru Public Health and Welfare Section)
